guide.summary: Linear documents OAuth2 for applications that act on behalf of individual users, and the confirmed read-only issue-title use case fits that model. The least-privilege documented grant is the default read scope, which is always present and gives read access to the authorizing user's account. Pagination is documented with first/after cursors on issues. Setup and execution are untested. Other workspaces connecting may need distribution review, which is not established by these sources.

findings.title: Use OAuth2 authorization-code flow with user actor for per-customer connections
findings.detail: Linear documents OAuth2 for applications integrating with Linear. The authorization URL takes client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope and state. The code is exchanged at the token endpoint, and the default actor is user, so resources are acted on as the authorizing user. This matches per-customer connections.

steps.title: Redirect the connecting user to Linear for read-only consent
steps.detail: Send the customer to the Linear authorization URL with response_type=code and scope=read (the default, always-present read scope). Do not request write, issues:create or admin. steps.title: Read the first page of issue titles
steps.detail: Query the GraphQL API with the access token to fetch the first 10 issues' titles and pageInfo. Expected output: a JSON response with issue nodes containing titles and pageInfo.hasNextPage and endCursor. Boundary check: request a non-issue read is not needed; instead confirm no mutation fields are used.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains issue title nodes and a pageInfo object.

evidence.quote: # Pagination All list responses from queries return paginated results. We implement Relay style cursor-based pagination model with `first`/`after` and `last`/`before` pagination arguments. For example, this is how to query
--data '{ "query": "{ issues { nodes { id title } } }" }' \
``` Or pass the token as an authorization header: `Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>`

request.example: curl '-X' 'POST' 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"query { issues(first: 10) { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }"}'

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: access_token from the token response for the connected test account

steps.title: Request the next page of issue titles using endCursor
steps.detail: Repeat the issues query using the endCursor from the previous response as the after argument, preserving first: 10. Repeat until pageInfo.hasNextPage is false; that is the documented end condition. This is a continuation of read-first-issue-titles.
steps.doneWhen: Each page's pageInfo.endCursor is passed as after until hasNextPage is false. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: } ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true
and you'll paginate through all the values in the collection.

request.example: curl '-X' 'POST' 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"query { issues(first: 10, after: \"<ENDCURSOR_FROM_PRIOR_RESPONSE>\") { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }"}'

fields: ENDCURSOR_FROM_PRIOR_RESPONSE: pageInfo.endCursor from the previous page, used as after
Access token: backend OAuth exchange for the test account; keep it out of this guide

steps.title: Continue issue title pagination until hasNextPage is false
steps.detail: Continue requesting pages with after set to the prior endCursor and first: 10 until pageInfo.hasNextPage is false. Stop only when hasNextPage is false.
steps.doneWhen: pageInfo.hasNextPage returns false on the final page and all titles were collected.
